abstract: We show that the Connes–Chamseddine spectral action and the associated noncommutative geometric formulation of the Standard Model arise as four-dimensional shadows of coherent fixed-point geometry under projection and truncation in Modal Triplet Theory (MTT). The almost-commutative spectral triple—including its finite algebra, fermionic Hilbert space, and Dirac operator—emerges as an effective encoding of coherent-sector overlap geometry. The cutoff scale and cutoff function of the spectral action are fixed (up to admissible reparametrization) by the coherent spectral gap and spectral proper-time (SPT) damping, eliminating their apparent arbitrariness. Gauge couplings, Yukawa matrices, and Higgs-sector parameters are not independently tunable within a coherent universality class, but are fixed functions of a single bottleneck vector \Theta that also controls collapse thresholds, spacetime event density, ultraviolet completion, and canonical geometric discreteness in independent shadow constructions. All results are slab-local and admissibility-conditioned.
